text: The thesis that a rational agent's credences must conform to the Kolmogorov probability axioms -- non-negativity, normalization (a tautology gets credence 1), and finite additivity -- is called ___.
explanation: Probabilism is the core Bayesian norm that rational credences obey the probability axioms: non-negativity (cr(P) >= 0), normalization (the credence in a tautology is 1), and finite additivity (cr(P v Q) = cr(P) + cr(Q) for mutually exclusive P, Q). It is standardly defended by the Dutch book argument and by accuracy-dominance (Joyce) arguments.
